definition: A legal basis under GDPR allowing organizations to process personal data when they have a genuine business need that doesn't override individuals' privacy rights.
metaDescription: Learn about legitimate interest under GDPR - when companies can use your data for business purposes without explicit consent and your rights.
simpleExplanation: Legitimate interest lets companies use your personal data for reasonable business purposes without asking permission first. However, your privacy rights must be balanced against their business needs, and you can object to this processing.
whyItMatters: Understanding legitimate interest helps you know when companies can legally use your data without consent and gives you the power to object when you disagree with their justification for processing your information.
technicalDetail: Under GDPR Article 6(1)(f), legitimate interest requires a three-part test: identifying a legitimate interest, showing processing is necessary for that interest, and conducting a balancing test to ensure individual rights aren't overridden. Organizations must document this assessment and inform data subjects of their right to object.

examples.explanation: A company monitors network traffic to detect cyber attacks, using employee data to protect the organization's systems and data security.
An online retailer sends product recommendations to past customers based on purchase history, claiming legitimate interest in customer relationship management.
A payment processor analyzes transaction patterns to identify potentially fraudulent activities, protecting both the business and other customers.
A news website tracks page views and user behavior to improve site performance and content, without using cookies that require consent.

niche: GDPR legal basis for data processing without explicit consent
